story_title: SPM-82: As Venue Staff, I want a tentative venue hold to expire if it is not confirmed in time so that a venue is not reserved indefinitely and becomes available for other requests.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every tentative hold has an expiry date and time, which is shown to the Event Coordinator and to Venue Staff.
The expiry is set when the hold is created, defaults to 7 days later, and can never be later than the start of the event.
Venue Staff can change a hold's expiry date and time while the hold is still active.
Given a hold has not been confirmed by its expiry date and time, when that time passes, then the hold's status changes to Expired.
An expired hold is not treated as a confirmed booking and cannot be approved; the Coordinator must submit a new request.
Given a hold has expired, when venue availability or conflicts are next checked, then the period it occupied, including the venue's setup and turnaround time, is available for other requests.
An expired hold is no longer shown as a hold on the venue availability calendar.
An expired hold remains on the event record and is distinguishable from pending, confirmed, rejected and withdrawn bookings.
The assigned Event Coordinator is notified a configurable period before a hold expires (default 24 hours) and again when it expires.
After a hold expires, the event's venue arrangement is shown as outstanding.

open_questions: DECIDED 2026-10-15 (the assumption in the story): a pending venue booking request is the tentative hold (discussion #41), and the hold is 'confirmed' when Venue Staff approve it. An approved booking never expires (AC11).

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (how expiry happens - the story's 'real unknown'): there is no scheduled job. Whenever bookings are read - the Venue tab, Venue Staff's Booking Requests, the availability calendar, venue search, a new request, an approval, Readiness, Confirm event, Submit for safety check - every pending hold whose expiry has passed is first marked Expired in one database statement, which also says which holds it changed, so each Coordinator is notified exactly once even if two people load a page at the same moment. The same check runs on every page change through the unread-notifications count, so warnings and expiry notices arrive while anyone is using the app. Discussion #55: notifications have no hard real-time requirement. A deployment can add a scheduled call later without changing any rule.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (AC2): the expiry is 7 days after the request, or the start of the event if that is sooner. For a multi-session event 'the start of the event' is the event's own start - its first session - so a later session's hold also expires by then at the latest.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (AC9, 'configurable'): there is no settings screen in the system (customer clarification on system configuration), so the warning period is the VENUE_HOLD_WARNING_HOURS setting in .env, default 24. The warning is sent once per hold; a hold already inside the period when it is created, or whose expiry is moved, is warned the next time bookings are read. It goes to the event's assigned Coordinator, or to whoever made the request if the event has none.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (wording): on the Coordinator's Venue tab a pending request reads 'Hold expires <date, time>' and an expired one has the badge 'Expired' and 'Hold expired on <date, time>'. Venue Staff's card has a 'Hold expires' row with a 'Change expiry' button; the form has 'New expiry', 'Save expiry' and 'Cancel'; success 'Hold expiry changed to <date, time>.'; refusals 'The expiry must be in the future.' and 'The expiry cannot be later than the start of the event (<date, time>).' Notifications: 'Venue hold expires soon' and 'Venue hold expired', each opening the event's Venue tab. Readiness and Confirm: 'the hold on <room> for this event expired on <date, time> - submit a new request'.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (AC10): an expired hold stays outstanding for its session until the Coordinator has a newer pending or approved request for the same space - the same session and, since SPM-90, the same purpose; a hold with no purpose recorded (made before SPM-90) is replaced by any newer request for its session - or marks it as not required (SPM-33). A rejected or withdrawn request still never counts. Found while running SPM-82-TC09: the purpose-only rule left an older hold outstanding after the Coordinator had re-requested the room.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (bookings made before SPM-82): the migration adds hold_expires_at and expiry_warning_sent_at to venue_bookings. Requests made through the app always get an expiry. Pending bookings already in the database, and ones that fixture scripts create directly, keep no expiry and never expire, so no other story's pending test bookings expire under its testers. Venue Staff can give such a hold an expiry with 'Change expiry'.

DECIDED 2026-10-15 (fixture dates): most cases use fixed dates - a hold that expired on 1 Oct 2026 stays expired. Three things are relative to when npm run fixtures:spm82 is run, because they are about time passing: the 7-day default (TC01), the cap at an event starting in 3 days (TC02) and the warning 12 hours before expiry (TC07).
RESOLVED 2026-10-15: changing the warning period from the screen, choosing email versus in-app delivery (#37) and holds on equipment are not part of this story.
